EXPLANATORY

NOTE

Transportation by rope aerially is another type of transportation system like railways, roads, etc. The passengers are transported by means of a carrier/carriers suspended on tensioned steel wire rope/wire ropes supported at intervals to limit sagging and thereby prevent passengers from touching the ground except at planned points. This is particularly useful in regions where the ability of surmounting natural barriers gives them a great advantage over railways and roads, both of which may need heavy civil engineering work to secure easy gradients. Aerial ropeways are inexpensive to maintain; their power demand is modest and they are It can negotiate valleys steep gradients, go in a not seriously affected by adverse climatic conditions. straight line and is limited only by storm conditions and visiblity. Since combinations are numerous depending upon various features, such as mode of transportation, purpose, topography of terrain, climatic conditions, etc, and finally one particular system will be suitable for a particular application, terrain and site conditions, the first step would be to collect the data and narrow down the choice. This part of the standard therefore, aims at listing the data to be supplied to the manufacturers In addition, inforby intending purchaser of an aerial system for transportation of passengers on surface. This information is required to be mation as given in Appendix A shall be provided to manufacturer. furnished as this has financial implications on the overall cost of project of aerial system. This standard is being issued in six parts which aim at listing the data to be supplied to the manufacturers by the intending purchasers of following types of aerial systems. Part Part Part Part Part Part I II I II IV V VI Transportation of goods Transportation of passengers, surface Transportation of passenger, underground Transportation of goods, underground Portable Forestry application
